en.title: Project Hail Mary's Rocky Eyeing Oscar Nod for Supporting Actor
en.summary: Amazon MGM Studios is making a bold play for Oscar recognition, submitting James Ortiz, the voice and puppeteer behind the beloved alien Rocky, for a Best Supporting Actor nomination. This marks a significant push to honor a non-human performance in a way the Academy rarely has.
en.body:
The buzz around **Project Hail Mary** is reaching a fever pitch, not just for its compelling narrative and scientific ingenuity, but for the potential for an unprecedented Oscar nomination. Amazon MGM Studios is reportedly championing **James Ortiz**, the brilliant mind behind the voice and puppetry of Rocky, for a Best Supporting Actor Academy Award. This move is a significant one, as the Oscars have historically been reluctant to recognize puppet performances, a hurdle that studios are now seemingly determined to overcome.

Rocky, the endearing, rock-like alien who forms an unlikely but profound friendship with **Ryan Gosling**'s Ryland Grace, has captured the hearts of audiences worldwide. Their shared mission to save their respective home worlds from a sun-devouring microbe creates a narrative of cosmic stakes and deeply personal connection. The studio is also submitting **Lionel Boyce**, who plays Grace's Earth-bound associate, for consideration in the same category, creating a fascinating duality in their campaign.

## A Surprising Oscar Contender

The push for Rocky’s nomination is more than just a studio’s ambitious marketing strategy; it’s a testament to the character’s impact and the exceptional craft involved in bringing him to life. Ortiz’s performance, seamlessly blending voice work with intricate puppetry, imbues Rocky with a personality, intelligence, and emotional depth that rivals many live-action performances. The Academy’s history with recognizing non-human characters in acting categories is sparse, with few exceptions often involving significant digital animation rather than practical puppetry. This makes the campaign for Rocky particularly noteworthy, potentially paving the way for future recognition of similar groundbreaking performances.

## What This Means for Fans

For the passionate fanbase of **Project Hail Mary**, this potential nomination is a cause for celebration and a validation of the film's unique magic. Readers and viewers have long championed Rocky as a standout character, praising the nuanced portrayal that made him feel as real and relatable as any human counterpart. The idea that such a beloved, non-human character could be recognized at the highest level of cinematic achievement is incredibly exciting. It speaks to the power of innovative storytelling and the dedication of artists like James Ortiz, whose work has elevated a science fiction adventure into something truly special that resonates deeply with its audience.

## What's Next

While the official Oscar nomination ballots are still some time away, this announcement signals a strong intent from Amazon MGM Studios. Fans will be eagerly watching the awards season unfold to see if Rocky, through James Ortiz's incredible performance, makes history. Further details regarding the studio's full Oscar submission slate are expected to be released soon.

Amaze! Amazon MGM Studios, like the rest of Hollywood, is putting forth its slate for Academy Award consideration , and for Project Hail Mary , they’re pushing for James Ortiz, the puppeteer and voice of the alien Rocky, to get a Best Supporting Actor nomination. Rocky, for those of you who haven’t had the pleasure, is the rock-alien whom Ryan Gosling’s Ryland Grace meets in the void of outer space. The two are both trying to find a solution to the microbe-like aliens eating their respective suns and form a lifelong friendship along the way. The Oscars have shied away from recognizing puppets with its awards; just ask Miss Piggy about it the next time you see her. But clearly the studio is making a push here, given the rightful popularity of the character. They’re also submitting Lionel Boyce, who plays Ryland Grace’s pal/security detail on Earth, for the category. Boyce and Ortiz are being submitted in just one of fifteen categories that the studio is submitting for Oscar consideration. The others are Best Actor for Gosling (of course), Best Supporting Actress for Sandra Hüller, Best Picture, Best Director, Best Adapted Screenplay, Best Cinematography, Best Editing, Best Casting, Best Production Design, Best Costume Design, Best Makeup and Hairstyling, Best Score, Best Sound, and Best Visual Effects. It will be interesting to see if the Academy picks up what Rocky is throwing down and awards Ortiz a nomination. Time will tell, and we can look up at the stars at night and contemplate life on other planets (or just watch Project Hail Mary again) while we wait to see how things shake out.
